title: Adaptive admission hysteresis & progressive circuit manager for token-level QoS
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Recent incidents showed noisy regional failover and repeated short-lived circuit flips when per-token admission thresholds are evaluated at region boundaries. Simple hard thresholds cause oscillation: regions rapidly open/close admission gates, triggering cascades and spurious failovers. Goal: implement an adaptive admission hysteresis layer plus a progressive circuit manager that ramps shedding at token granularity and coordinates across regions to reduce flapping while preserving SLOs.
motivation: Reduce operational noise and customer-visible latency spikes during partial region overloads. Improve predictability of multi-region failover decisions and make shedding decisions reversible with graceful ramp-down rather than binary open/close transitions.
design_summary: 1) Admission hysteresis: per-shard token admit counters maintain smoothed admit ratios with configurable decay windows (e.g., EMA over configurable token counts). Hysteresis introduces separate open/close thresholds with a minimum dwell time to avoid rapid toggles. 2) Progressive circuit manager: instead of a single circuit state, circuits expose discrete progress levels (NORMAL -> CONSERVE -> AGGRESSIVE -> OPEN) with token-level target admit percentages. Transition rules use combined signals: sustained p95/p99 latency, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, and cross-region sibling load indications. 3) Coordination: regions publish compact control messages (region health vectors) to a lightweight coordination topic; progressive manager uses quorum-like heuristics to prefer localized shedding but can escalate globally when cross-region spill is detected. 4) Observability: new golden-signal panels and token-level SLI histograms, plus a "circuit ladder" visualization showing progression and time-in-state per region.
acceptance_criteria: Hysteresis implemented as configurable module; default decay window = 60s and dwell time = 30s
Progressive circuit exposes 4 states with documented admit targets and transition conditions
Metrics emitted: admit_ratio, admit_target, dwell_time_remaining, state_transitions_count, progressive_level per shard/region
Grafana dashboard panels for: token admit heatmap, progressive level timelines per region, p95/p99 vs admit_ratio correlation
Synthetic traffic chaos tests demonstrate reduction in oscillation: state-flip frequency reduced by >= 70% under staged overload compared to baseline
Failover playbook updated with new runbook steps and automated rollback hooks
implementation_notes: Add AdmissionHysteresis class to runtime admission path; keep CPU cost O(1) per request by updating compact EMA counters only on admit/deny events
ProgressiveCircuitManager pluggable strategy: default 'latency-first' uses p99 nasalized gradient, optional 'capacity-first' for enterprise customers
Coordination channel: reuse existing regional control topic (kafka/control-v2) with compact protobuf schema; keep message sizes < 256 bytes
Avoid strong cross-region synchronization to prevent cascading RPCs; use eventual convergence with grace periods
Expose feature flag to flip between legacy boolean circuit and progressive manager for canary rollout
telemetry_spec: span: runtime.admit_evaluation (tags: region, shard, model, route)
event: runtime.prog_circuit_escalation (payload: reason, p99, kv_hit_rate, sibling_signals)
log: admit_decision (sampled, include tokenized request id, decision_reason)
dashboards: Grafana: 'Progressive Circuit Ladder' - timeline of levels across regions with dwell times
Grafana: 'Admit Heatmap' - heatmap of admit_ratio by shard x time + anomaly overlays
Grafana: 'Latency vs Admit' - scatter and correlation panels showing token p95/p99 vs admit_ratio
Grafana: 'State Transition SLO' - counters and rates for transitions by cause
Playbook notebook: 'regional_admit_retrospective' with synthetic test artifacts and comparison plots
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag behind runtime-experiments: default OFF in prod
2) Canary on 1 region (staging-1) for 48h with synthetic spike harness and synthetic KV hit variation
3) Measure state-flip frequency and p99; threshold: p99 regressions <= 5% and flip frequency reduced >= 50%
4) Ramp to 3 regions with monitoring alerts enabled; keep legacy boolean fallback enabled
5) Full global rollout only after 7-day stability window and sign-off from reliability and oncall owners
test_plan: Unit tests for hysteresis decay, dwell time enforcement, and state transitions
Integration tests for coordination messages and graceful degradation when control topic unavailable
Chaos test: gradual 2x token rate increase in region-A to verify progressive ramp and reduced spill to region-B
A/B experiment: compare baseline circuits vs progressive manager under tiered traffic mix (LLM interactive vs batch)
